description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a model, likely in the context of feedback incorporation. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," is linear and ranges from approximately 0.81 to 0.99, with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also linear and spans from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The blue line with solid circles represents "Final Accuracy," starting at approximately 1.0, dipping slightly to around 0.92 near 0.87, then rising again to a final value of about 0.99 at 0.99. The orange line with diamond markers represents "Δ Accuracy," beginning at about 0.45, declining to a low of approximately 0.10 near 0.87, and then rising to about 0.20 before falling to near 0.0 at 0.99. The green line with square markers represents "Initial Accuracy," starting at about 0.55, rising to a peak of approximately 0.85 near 0.89, then declining slightly to around 0.75 before rising again to about 0.98 at 0.99. All lines are plotted with error bars indicating variability.
